payload.rebuttal: argued: The mutant removes the `row["state"] != "ORPHANED"` guard from `owned_urls`'s set comprehension, but that guard is reached only inside the `else` branch, which runs exactly when `orphaned_with_url` is empty. `orphaned_with_url` is built from every row in `rows` whose state is `ORPHANED` and whose url is non-empty, so an empty `orphaned_with_url` already means no `ORPHANED` row in `rows` carries a non-empty url. Dropping the `!= "ORPHANED"` filter can only add ORPHANED rows' urls to `owned_urls`, and every one of those is the empty string by the time this line runs, which the set comprehension's own truthiness check already excludes. So the two versions compute the identical set on every reachable input: this is an equivalent mutant, not a gap in test coverage, and no test can kill it without first removing the earlier `if orphaned_with_url:` branch. I added a two-line comment at the mutated site documenting this invariant, so a future reader or refactor does not mistake the filter for dead weight to delete, but no behavioral fix is possible or needed.
